title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Architecture
text: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pairs a non-parametric document retriever with a language model so answers are conditioned on up-to-date external evidence rather than parametric memory alone. By retrieving relevant passages at query time, RAG reduces factual hallucinations and supports traceable source citations. Modern production RAG systems combine lexical retrieval, dense vector search, rank fusion, and cross-encoder re-ranking before generating or extracting final answers.

title: Okapi BM25 Sparse Retrieval
text: Okapi BM25 is a probabilistic lexical ranking function that scores documents based on query term frequency, inverse document frequency (IDF), and document length normalization. Standard Okapi BM25 uses tuning parameters k1=1.5 to control term frequency saturation and b=0.75 to scale document length relative to the average corpus length. Because BM25 operates on exact token matches, it excels at rare identifiers, acronyms, error codes, and proper nouns where dense embeddings can lose precision.

title: Dense Vector Retrieval and Bi-Encoders
text: Dense retrieval encodes queries and corpus passages into fixed-dimensional vectors and ranks passages using L2-normalized cosine similarity or inner product. Bi-encoder architectures embed the query and each passage independently, allowing document vectors to be precomputed and indexed offline for sub-millisecond lookup. Even lightweight TF-IDF L2-normalized vector spaces capture weighted term profiles, while neural embedding backends add semantic synonym matching.

title: Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) for Hybrid RAG
text: Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) merges ranked lists from heterogeneous retrievers such as sparse BM25 and dense vector search without requiring score calibration or normalization across incompatible scales. For each document, RRF sums 1 / (k + rank) across every retriever that returns it, using a standard smoothing constant of k=60 to prevent top-ranked outliers from dominating. As a result, documents retrieved strongly by both sparse and dense methods receive a compounded boost over single-retriever hits, improving recall and robustness in hybrid RAG.

title: Cross-Encoder Re-Ranking
text: Cross-encoder re-rankers jointly evaluate a query and a candidate passage together rather than encoding them separately like bi-encoders. By attending across query and passage tokens simultaneously, a cross-encoder captures exact phrase alignment, term coverage, bigram proximity, and IDF-weighted overlap at higher precision. Because joint scoring is computationally heavier than first-stage retrieval, pipelines apply re-ranking only to the top candidate pool produced by BM25, dense search, or RRF.

title: Document Chunking Strategies and Overlap
text: Document chunking splits long sources into coherent passages sized to fit embedding and context limits without diluting semantic focus. Fixed-token sliding windows typically retain 10% to 20% overlap between adjacent chunks so sentences spanning boundaries remain intact. Structure-aware chunkers preserve markdown headings, paragraphs, and table boundaries to keep logical context together during retrieval.

title: Citation Grounding and Attribution
text: Citation grounding links generated or extracted answer statements directly to supporting source passages using inline identifiers such as [doc_id]. Sentence-level attribution inspects lexical overlap, key term coverage, and semantic alignment between each answer sentence and retrieved evidence. Measuring groundedness helps verify that every claim presented to users is backed by retrieved context rather than fabricated.

title: Query Expansion and HyDE
text: Query expansion improves recall when user questions are terse or phrased differently from corpus documents. Hypothetical Document Embeddings (HyDE) prompts a model to draft a plausible answer passage first and embeds that synthetic passage to search the vector index. Combining expanded queries with sparse BM25 keywords helps bridge vocabulary gaps without discarding exact technical terms.

title: HNSW and Approximate Nearest Neighbor Indexing
text: Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) graphs enable fast approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search over millions of L2-normalized dense embeddings. HNSW builds multi-layer proximity graphs where upper layers provide long-range skips and lower layers refine local neighborhoods. Tuning efSearch and M trades off index memory and build time against high recall@10 at low query latency.

title: Faithfulness and Hallucination Detection
text: Faithfulness evaluation checks whether every atomic claim in an answer is entailed by the retrieved reference passages. Claim-level verifiers inspect numeric consistency, negation polarity, and entity overlap to flag unsupported or contradicted assertions. High retrieval recall alone cannot prevent hallucinations unless downstream grounding and faithfulness checks audit the final output.

title: Context Window Management and Lost-in-the-Middle
text: Language models exhibit the lost-in-the-middle phenomenon where facts placed in the middle of long prompts receive less attention than items at the beginning or end. Placing highest-scoring re-ranked passages first and deduplicating redundant chunks maximizes evidence density within tight token budgets. Filtering irrelevant candidates prior to prompt assembly directly improves downstream answer accuracy.

title: Information Retrieval Evaluation Metrics
text: Standard retrieval benchmarks measure system quality using Recall@K, Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR), and Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain (NDCG). Recall@K tracks whether relevant evidence appears anywhere in the top K passages, while MRR rewards placing the first relevant hit at rank 1. NDCG@K handles graded relevance labels and discounts results appearing further down the ranked list.

title: TF-IDF Weighting and Sublinear Term Scaling
text: Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) weights words by balancing how often a term appears in a document against how rare it is across the corpus. Applying sublinear term frequency scaling such as 1 + log(tf) dampens repetitive words while L2 normalization ensures longer documents do not dominate cosine similarity. Unigram and bigram TF-IDF vectors provide a strong, deterministic baseline for dense retrieval tests.

title: Semantic Caching and Latency Optimization
text: Production RAG pipelines reduce serving latency and compute cost by caching normalized query embeddings, first-stage retrieval lists, and re-ranked answers. Semantic caches match incoming queries against recent embeddings above a strict cosine similarity threshold such as 0.95. Pairing deterministic local re-ranking with cached corpus indexes keeps end-to-end retrieval predictable and fast.
